headline: Adding AGT-a48565d1-1 to 1 existing rule(s) changed held-out rule-set recall by +5.4 pp and false-positive rate by +0.21 pp (+23 alerts). Awaiting human review.

advisory.title: Preventing Card Testing: Spot It Early, Stop It Fast
advisory.rights_note: Short attributed excerpts quoted for analysis; full text remains at the source URL.
advisory.excerpt:
Card testing is when fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions.
Fraud tactics are evolving, and card testing attacks are increasingly targeting e-commerce and mobile checkout.
They run $0 or small-dollar attempts at real merchants to confirm a card is active and may retry to fill in missing details (like CVV or expiration date).
Automated testing is the most common.
Many different card numbers attempted in a short time—often from the same IP address, device or small set of sessions.
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors.
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time (for example, cycling CVV or expiration date values).
A wave of $0 authorizations or low-dollar transactions used to test cards with minimal cost and attention.

dataset.description: Synthetic payments scenario (~3.4% fraud) with velocity, decline, card-present, time-of-day, device, SIM-change, credential-reset, and new-payee features. Three fraud modes: high-value misuse, injected card testing, and injected SIM-swap account takeover.
dataset.limitations: Fully synthetic. The card-testing and SIM-swap account-takeover patterns were injected to demonstrate how the workflow surfaces coverage gaps, and legitimate look-alikes were added for each; results do not measure real-world detection.

findings.summary: Card testing attacks involve fraudsters testing stolen card credentials using $0 or low-dollar transactions and repeated rapid attempts. While IP address and device ID fields are missing from the schema, transaction velocity (transactions_1h) and amount can be used to detect these patterns.
behaviors: Fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions.
Many different card numbers attempted in a short time.
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors.
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time.
indicators: High velocity of attempts in a short time window
Repeated declined attempts or CVV/expiration mismatch errors
testable_hypotheses: Transactions with high velocity and very low amounts indicate card testing activity.
Combining high velocity, low amount, and prior declined attempts improves precision for card testing detection.
uncertainties: The dataset lacks explicit IP address and device identifier fields, limiting detection to transaction-level velocity proxies.
Synthetic test data may not reflect sophisticated distributed botnet card testing dynamics.

agent_conclusion.rationale: The intelligence document highlights card testing attacks via $0 or low-dollar transactions and rapid authorization attempts. Using available proxy fields (transactions_1h and amount), candidate rule AGT-a48565d1-1 successfully identified a detection gap and increased recall on the validation split from 32.51% to 40.39% with a modest increase in false positives.
limitations: IP address and device identifier fields are not present in the dataset schema, requiring reliance on transaction velocity and amount proxies.
Synthetic data distribution may not fully capture complex card testing browser fingerprinting patterns.

rule.name: Rapid Low Dollar Transactions Card Testing
rule.rationale: Detects card testing attacks characterized by multiple transactions in a short time window (transactions_1h >= 5) with small-dollar amounts (amount < 5).

rule.name: High Velocity Low Amount with Declines
rule.rationale: Captures rapid attempts combined with low dollar amounts and prior declined authorization attempts indicating card testing.

baseline_rule.name: High transaction amount baseline
baseline_rule.description: Flags a transaction when its amount is at least 1,500 synthetic currency units.
